tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. name: dg-obsidian-cdp-verify
description: Verify Obsidian plugin changes by driving the running app over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and asserting on real behaviour. Use when a change needs proving in the real app rather than by unit test — apps/obsidian has no test runner — or when a reviewer asks "does this actually work?".
---

# DG Obsidian CDP Verify

Use this skill to prove an `apps/obsidian` change works in a real Obsidian vault.

`apps/obsidian` has no test runner (roam, website, database and content-model do).
The way to prove a change works is to drive the real app: Obsidian is Electron, so
it speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol. About 150 lines covers `evaluate`, input
injection and condition polling — Playwright is not required.

## Prerequisites

1. **Relaunch Obsidian with the debug port.** Run the steps separately — the
   auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound command.
   ```bash
   osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to quit'
   ```
   ```bash
   open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222
   ```
   Ask the user before doing this: it closes their running app.
2. **Your build in the vault.** `apps/obsidian/.env` mirrors the dev build into
   the vault plugin dir. Confirm it is _your_ build — see the first gotcha.

## Quick Start

```sh
# 1. preflight: port up, right vault, YOUR bundle, plugin enabled
node skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/preflight.mjs "a string unique to your change"

# 2. run a verification
node skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs
```

Set `VAULT` to target a vault other than `testVault`.

Write the verification as scenarios and hand them to `runVerification`, which owns
everything order-dependent (plugin reload, stray-modal cleanup, teardown, exit
code):

```js
import { runVerification } from "./scripts/harness.mjs";

await runVerification({
  modalSelector: ".dg-node-search-modal",
  setup: async ({ client }) => ({
    /* snapshot anything you will mutate */
  }),
  teardown: async ({ client, state }) => {
    /* put it back */
  },
  scenarios: [
    {
      name: "01-does-the-thing",
      body: async ({ client, check, state }) => {
        await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById("…");`);
        await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".my-modal")`, {
          label: "modal",
        });
        check(
          "the thing happened",
          await client.evaluate(`…`),
          "detail on failure",
        );
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

`client` gives you `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `reloadPlugin` and
`pressEscape`. See `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` — the real
verification that shipped ENG-2114 (15 assertions, 3 scenarios). Copy it as the
starting point for a new one.

## Gotchas

Each of these cost real debugging time. The second and third produced confident,
wrong diagnoses that survived until they were deliberately tested.

| Symptom                                               | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "My feature is missing from the build"                | **Every worktree's dev watcher mirrors into the same vault plugin dir.** Another branch's watcher silently overwrote your bundle. This is what `preflight.mjs` checks. Find competing watchers with `pgrep -fl "scripts/dev.ts"`; rebuild with `(cd apps/obsidian && pnpm build)`. |
| App appears to double-handle one keypress             | Your key helper spread `{ type, ...opts }`, so a caller's `type: "keyDown"` overrode the loop and sent two keydowns. `type` must come **after** the spread.                                                                                                                        |
| `editor.hasFocus()` is false but focus looks right    | CodeMirror ANDs with `document.hasFocus()`, so it reports false whenever Obsidian is not the frontmost macOS app — running a build in the terminal flips it. Assert `document.activeElement.closest(".cm-editor")` instead.                                                        |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks correct    | Obsidian saves on a debounce. Poll the file until it changes; never read straight after the action.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Assertions read a mix of two modals                   | A crashed earlier run left one mounted. `runVerification` clears strays first; a synthetic `body.click()` will not dismiss a modal, an Escape key event will.                                                                                                                      |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found"           | You detached every markdown leaf first. Use `getLeaf("tab")`, which reuses an empty active leaf.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Editing only files under `src/styles/` never rebuilds | The concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd`, outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Top-level `await` throws inside `evaluate`            | Bodies are wrapped in a plain function. Return a promise chain instead.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Wrong window driven                                   | Several page targets exist — one per open vault, plus popouts and settings. Select by `app.vault.getName()`, never by title.                                                                                                                                                       |

Two more, from experience rather than symptoms:

- **Reset state at the start of a scenario**, or assertions inherit leftover tabs
  and splits from the last run and a correct implementation reads as a failure.
- **The developer is using the app while you drive it.** A human opening a tab
  mid-run produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation.

## Safety Notes

- Ask before relaunching Obsidian: it closes the app the developer is using.
- Verification runs mutate the vault — scratch notes, sometimes app settings.
  Snapshot anything you change in `setup` and restore it in `teardown`.
- Point runs at a dev vault (`testVault`), never a real one.

=== reference_obsidian_cdp_driving.md
---
name: reference-obsidian-cdp-driving
description: "How to drive the running Obsidian app programmatically over CDP to verify plugin changes, and where the fuller Playwright harness lives"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01fc3963-d706-437b-b51d-c4c4cfa1c803
  modified: 2026-09-08T01:24:16.291Z
---

Obsidian is Electron, so it can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Relaunch with
`open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222`, then attach over
`ws` to the target from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`. Verified working August 2026 on
Obsidian 1.8.4 / macOS — 23/23 assertions driving the ENG-2113 search footer.

Key points learned the hard way:

- **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  to select one. The rewrite is how PR #959 selects a vault and it is also that PR's worst bug —
  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- **Force the renderer active over CDP instead of fighting for window focus.** Two calls at connect
  time make occlusion throttling irrelevant:
  `Page.setWebLifecycleState {state:"active"}` and `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled {enabled:true}`.
  Without them, `osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to activate'` only holds until the next
  command returns focus to the terminal, and Reading view silently renders an **empty**
  `.markdown-preview-section` — links, Properties and backlinks all absent, no error. Verified
  September 2026 on Obsidian 1.13.7: the identical scenario went from `body link rendered: false`
  to `true` with those two calls added. The note below still describes the underlying throttling.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.
  ENG-2107 lost an hour to this. Check `visibilityState` and a 100 ms timer's real latency before
  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,
  so ask the user to click the window and poll `visibilityState` before firing the scenario.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.
- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain
  `editor.focus()` with no modal involved and `document.hasFocus() === true`; no element holds DOM
  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*
  modal — producing "footer missing the action" and "modal did not close" failures while the feature
  actually works. Start every scenario with
  `document.querySelectorAll(".modal-container").forEach(el => el.remove())`.
- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the
  folder name to `disablePlugin`/`enablePlugin` silently no-ops (`loaded: false`, `manifests[folder]`
  undefined). Read the real id from `app.plugins.manifests`, whose `dir` field maps id → folder.

- `detachLeavesOfType("markdown")` followed by `getLeaf(true)` throws **"No tab group found."** —
  detaching the last markdown leaf destroys the tab group the new leaf would go in. Reuse
  `getMostRecentLeaf()` instead of clearing first.
- Obsidian's **Properties** block and the **backlinks-in-document** panel contain **no
  `a.internal-link` anchors**: a link property renders as `div.multi-select-pill-content.internal-link`
  and backlink entries carry no anchors at all. A markdown post processor that queries
  `a.internal-link` therefore cannot leak into either, whatever it scans. Both panels are also
  collapsed/`display:none` by default, so a scenario must expand Properties
  (`.metadata-properties-heading`) and run `backlink:toggle-backlinks-in-document` before asserting.
- **A markdown post processor receives its element DETACHED (`el.isConnected === false`) during a
  normal Reading view render**, but attached and inside `.modal-container` when the plugin calls
  `MarkdownRenderer.render` itself. So `el.closest(".markdown-reading-view")` is null on the real
  path and is the wrong guard; `el.closest(".modal-container")` is the correct tell for "this is our
  own modal preview". Measured with a throwaway `registerMarkdownPostProcessor` probe pushing to a
  `window.__probe` array — a cheap pattern for any question about post processor call context.
- zsh expands `${VAR}` inside `node -e "..."`, silently turning `plugins['${ID}']` into `plugins['']`.
  Write the scenario to a `.mjs` file instead of passing it through `-e`.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with
CHANGES_REQUESTED — the blocking objection is documentation quality, not the mechanism — and is far
behind main. Reuse its `e2e/helpers/obsidian-setup.ts` rather than rediscovering the launch tricks.

Unrelated dev-loop gotcha hit while doing this: editing only a file under `apps/obsidian/src/styles/`
never triggers a rebuild, because the concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd` while those files sit
outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file to force it. See [[feedback-obsidian-no-console]] for the
related Notice-instead-of-console rule in this app.
=== reference_obsidian_contested_vault_plugin_dir.md
---
name: reference-obsidian-contested-vault-plugin-dir
description: "A dev watcher in another worktree overwrites the shared vault plugin dir mid-session; grep the mirrored bundle for a symbol you just added before trusting any verification"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Every worktree's `apps/obsidian` dev watcher mirrors to the **same** vault plugin directory
(`<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`). With watchers running in several worktrees, one
of them rebuilding replaces your `main.js` at any moment — including *between* two CDP
verification runs.

Observed on ENG-2231: verification passed, then the next run reported zero decorations and a
missing injected `<style>`. Cause was not the code — a watcher in
`eng-1249-...-overlay-feature` had re-mirrored its own build, and the vault's `main.js` again
contained `TagNodeHandler`, the class the change had just deleted.

**Check before believing any live result:**

```bash
V=<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs
ps aux | grep "[s]cripts/dev.ts"          # who else is watching
grep -c "<symbol you just added>" $V/main.js
grep -c "<symbol you just deleted>" $V/main.js   # must be 0
```

Prefer a one-shot `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<vault path> npx tsx scripts/build.ts` chained in the
**same command** as the verification, rather than a long-lived watcher, so the window for another
watcher to clobber it is as small as possible.

Related: [[reference-obsidian-shared-plugin-mirror]], [[reference-obsidian-cdp-driving]].
=== reference_obsidian_shared_plugin_mirror.md
---
name: reference-obsidian-shared-plugin-mirror
description: "Every worktree's obsidian dev watcher mirrors into the same vaults via OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH, so concurrent watchers overwrite each other"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`apps/obsidian/.env` sets `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` to absolute vault paths
(`testVault`, `testVault2`), and every worktree gets a copy of that `.env`. So two
worktrees running `turbo dev --filter=@discourse-graphs/obsidian` at once both
mirror their build into the *same* `.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs/` — last
write wins, and a verification run can silently exercise another branch's code.

Before trusting any runtime verification, grep the mirrored bundle for a string
unique to the change:

```bash
grep -c "insert link at cursor" /Users/trang.doan/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs/main.js
```

**Each worktree's `.env` can point at a different vault**, so "which watcher is
fighting me" is not guessable — read it. August 2026: eng-2110 targeted
`testVault2` while eng-2111 targeted `testVault`.

```bash
grep -o "OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH.*" .claude/worktrees/<branch>/apps/obsidian/.env
```

`pgrep -fl "scripts/dev.ts"` **misses these watchers** — `turbo dev` spawns
esbuild directly, so nothing matches `scripts/dev.ts` and the check reports a
clean machine while two watchers are live. Match on the worktree path instead:

```bash
ps aux | grep -iE "[e]sbuild|turbo.*[d]ev" | grep worktrees
```

Seen August 2026 with the eng-2110 and eng-2111 watchers both live while
verifying eng-2112.

See [[reference-obsidian-cdp-driving]] for driving the app itself.
=== reference_obsidian_escape_keymap_scope.md
---
name: reference-obsidian-escape-keymap-scope
description: "Escape inside an Obsidian Modal cannot be intercepted from the DOM — push a keymap scope instead"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

A React handler inside an Obsidian `Modal` cannot stop Escape from closing the
modal. Obsidian registers its close-on-Escape before any plugin React tree
exists, so a listener added later always runs second. Verified empirically on
Obsidian 1.13.7, August 2026:

- `event.preventDefault()` + `event.nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation()` in a
  React bubble handler — modal still closes.
- A **capture**-phase `keydown` listener on `window` that stops the event — fires,
  logs, and the modal still closes. Obsidian's listener is registered earlier, so
  ordering within the same phase goes to Obsidian.
- `this.scope.register([], "Escape", …)` on the Modal's own scope — also loses.
  `Modal`'s constructor registered Escape on that scope first, and `Scope`
  resolves handlers in registration order rather than reverse.

What works is pushing a scope, which is public API (`Keymap.pushScope` /
`Keymap.popScope`) and lands above the modal in the stack:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isOpen) return;
  const scope = new Scope();
  scope.register([], "Escape", () => {
    onOpenChange(false);
    return false; // false auto-preventDefaults
  });
  app.keymap.pushScope(scope);
  return () => app.keymap.popScope(scope);
}, [app, isOpen, onOpenChange]);
```

Keep this inside the dropdown/popover component so each one owns its own Escape
and no state has to be plumbed back into the `Modal` subclass. Other keys are a
different problem: React-level `stopPropagation()` on the panel container is
still what keeps Enter and the arrows away from an ancestor's result navigation.

Implemented in `apps/obsidian/src/components/SearchDropdown.tsx` (ENG-2112). The
same bug is confirmed present in ENG-2110's `NodeTypeFilterMenu`.
See [[reference-obsidian-cdp-driving]] for how this was verified.
=== reference_cm6_decorations_not_dom_stamping.md
---
name: reference-cm6-decorations-not-dom-stamping
description: "Never style CodeMirror-owned spans by stamping attributes from a MutationObserver; use a CM6 decoration — CM recreates those elements on focus and on scroll"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

In Obsidian's editor, anything that styles CodeMirror's own elements (hashtags, links,
formatting spans) MUST be a CM6 `Decoration` from a `ViewPlugin`, never attributes stamped
onto the DOM from a `MutationObserver`.

**The mechanism is attribute re-sync, not element recreation.** Root-caused on ENG-2231 by
monkey-patching `Element.prototype.removeAttribute` and capturing a stack when the attributes
vanished, which pointed at `t.sync` recursing through `app://obsidian.md/app.js` — CodeMirror's
`ContentView.sync()`, bundled into Obsidian. It walks the view tree and re-applies each
element's attributes **from its decoration spec, deleting any it does not own**. The spans stay
the same DOM nodes: the tag-span count held at 4 while the coloured count went 4 to 0, and the
removals arrived in exact reverse insertion order.

Separately, line DOM really is dropped and rebuilt as the viewport scrolls (measured: 55 of 136
lines rendered), so scrolling defeats outside stamping too.

No tightening of observer filters fixes this; the plugin is racing the framework's own
attribute bookkeeping.

**Diagnostic technique worth reusing:** patch `removeAttribute` (or the relevant setter) and
capture `new Error().stack` to find who is really mutating the DOM. Reasoning from
MutationObserver output alone produced two confident wrong answers here — first "CodeMirror
recreates the spans", then "the plugin's own cleanup removes them" — before the stack named the
real caller. A plugin-disabled control run is also essential: it showed hand-stamped attributes
surviving the identical action, which is what ruled the plugin in, and then out.

Use `syntaxTree(view.state).iterate()` rather than regex-matching `#tag` in the raw text —
Obsidian's own rules for what counts as a tag (fenced/inline code, URL fragments, `# heading`)
are then inherited for free. Verified: all four are correctly left undecorated.
Obsidian derives a hashtag's CSS classes from its syntax node name, so the node name carries
the tag as a `tag-<name>` segment, e.g. `hashtag_hashtag-end_meta_tag-clm-candidate`.

**A mark decoration can only create a span INSIDE Obsidian's own `.cm-hashtag` span, never on
it.** The outer span owns the tag pill — measured `border-radius: 28px`, `padding: 3.5px 0 3.5px
9.1px`, height 24px vs the inner text's 17px — so colouring the decoration itself paints only the
glyph box and leaves a visible ring of the theme's colour around it. Reach back up to the parent
with `:has()` instead, from a generated stylesheet keyed on a per-node class:

```css
span.cm-hashtag:has(> .dg-tag-<nodeId>) { background-color: X; color: Y; }
```

No `!important` needed: Obsidian's own rule is a bare `.cm-hashtag { background: var(--tag-background) }`
(0,1,0) and themes recolour tags by redefining that variable rather than adding stronger
selectors, so (0,2,1) wins. A generated stylesheet must be injected per document — popout windows
have their own and the bundled `styles.css` does not carry into them.

Working reference implementations in the repo: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/discourseTagExtension.ts`
and `wikilinkDragHandler.ts`. See [[reference-obsidian-cdp-driving]] for verifying this live.
=== reference_cm6_widget_ignore_event.md
---
name: reference-cm6-widget-ignore-event
description: "CM6 WidgetType.ignoreEvent() defaults to true, which is what a clickable widget wants; returning false breaks its own click handler"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

CodeMirror 6's `WidgetType.ignoreEvent()` reads backwards. It answers "should the **editor** ignore
this event?", not "should the widget ignore it".

- `true` (the default) → the editor stays out of the way, and the widget's own DOM listeners fire
  normally. **This is what you want for an interactive widget** — a button, a badge, a drag handle.
- `false` → CM routes the event through its own input handling, and the widget's `addEventListener`
  handler never runs.

Overriding it to `false` "so the widget can receive clicks" is the intuitive-but-wrong move; it
produces a widget that renders correctly and silently does nothing on click. Hit in ENG-1249 on the
Obsidian discourse context badge; `apps/obsidian/src/utils/wikilinkDragHandler.ts` already had the
correct default and a comment explaining it.

---
name: pr-evidence
description: Upload verification screenshots to the Roam dev graph and get public image URLs plus a Markdown table for the PR body. Use after a verification run produced PNGs and before create-pr writes the Evidence section.
---

# PR evidence upload

Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section.

## When to use

- After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk.
- Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`.

## Command

Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \
  [--slot N] [--branch <b>] [--label "<YYYY-MM-DD · shortsha · harness>"] [--harness <name>] \
  [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \
  shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ...
```

- `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths.
- `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to `<today> · <short sha> · <--harness or "manual">`.
- Caption defaults to the file name without extension.
- No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error.
- Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch).

## Output contract

- stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`.
- stderr: `Markdown table: <path>`. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-<runBlockUid>.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is.
- URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23).

## Roam structure

```
Trang test/                       (page, found or created)
  <branch>                        (top-level block, reused on every run)
    <date · sha · harness>        (new run block per invocation, appended last)
      <caption> ![](<url>)        (one per PNG)
```

## Gotchas

- Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<n>` is set.
- A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files.
- Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun.
- Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`.
- Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run.
- tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.

---
name: dg-obsidian-cdp-verify
description: Prove an apps/obsidian change works in the real Obsidian app by driving it over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. One command launches or attaches to Obsidian on a test vault slot, builds this worktree into it, runs scenario modules, and writes a scenario matrix plus screenshots for pr-evidence and create-pr. Use for live Obsidian verification before a PR, or when asked "does this actually work in Obsidian?".
---

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --slot 1 --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- Slots come from `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It takes a JSON array or a comma list of plugin dirs or vault roots. `--slot N` is 1-based and defaults to 1.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved slot, the lock and the Obsidian state. If another live run holds the lock, it exits 2 and asks you to switch slot. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about competing `dev.ts`/esbuild watchers. Your own worktree's watcher counts too, if it mirrors into the same vault.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| Styles-only edit not in the build | Files under `src/styles/` sit outside esbuild's module graph. Touch a `.ts` file. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |

62	  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
63	  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
64	};
65	```
66	
67	- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
68	- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
69	- The harness does these for you:
70	  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
71	  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
72	  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
73	- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).
74	
75	## Evidence
76	
77	- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
78	- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
79	- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:
80	
81	```sh
82	./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
83	```
84	
85	## Cleanup
86	
87	- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
88	- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
89	- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.
90	
91	## Gotchas
92	
93	These are the ones the code can't handle for you.
94	
95	| Symptom | Cause / fix |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
98	| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
99	| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
100	| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
101	| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
102	| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
103	| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
104	| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
105	| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
106	| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
107	| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
108	| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |

Phase 3 is built and all eight checks passed. The ported ENG-2114 insert-link scenario passes 3/3 on current main after one selector fix: the search box is now a text-editable element, not an `<input>`. Obsidian is left running with the debug port, and the repo's git status is unchanged.

**How to run it**, from the worktree root:
```
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs --slot 1 --marker "<str>" --scenario a.mjs [--scenario b.mjs] [--skip-build]
```
It prints the `last-run.json` path, the timings, the `| Scenario | Input | Expected | Actual | Pass |` table and the screenshot args for pr-evidence. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 a scenario failed, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

**Checks**

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Port the insert-link scenario | 3 scenarios pass: wikilink, markdown link, and the insert action absent with no note open. |
| 2 | Obsidian running without the port | It quit Obsidian (pid 51094 → 84330), relaunched with the port and opened dgDevVault. Launch 1.6s, build 2.7s, total 5.1s. The scenarios failed on this run because of the selector drift; after the fix every later run passed. |
| 3 | Run again | Attached without relaunching. Launch 0.33s, total 7.1s. |
| 4 | Marker that doesn't exist | Deliver stopped with a clear "PREFLIGHT FAIL" message, exit 3. `run.mjs` stopped before any scenario and released the lock. |
| 5 | Lock held by a fake live process | Doctor and `run.mjs` both exit 2 with "…being driven by pid 87226 on branch fake-other-run… Switch vault: rerun with --slot <1..3> other than 1." The run left the foreign lock alone; I removed my fake lock afterwards. |
| 6 | Obsidian not running | Launched with the port, 3/3 pass. Launch 1.0s, total 8.7s. |
| 7 | Upload through pr-evidence | Uploaded under `Trang test/` → `cdp-verify-smoke`. Table: `local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/main/2026-09-23T21-18-26/pr-evidence-Qw6KPNRxs.md` |
| 8 | Vault before/after | The only new file is `_verify/main/insert-link-scratch.md`; nothing was deleted. |

The three uploaded screenshots:
- [Insert wikilink](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-dev-graph%2FbIPRQj8Sjm.png?alt=media&token=402773ef-9c73-4bac-a6ee-8e656a75f130)

In check 8, some `.obsidian/*.json` files have newer timestamps: `app.json`, `types.json`, `core-plugins.json`, `community-plugins.json`, `appearance.json` and a dictionary plugin's `data.json`. The scenarios change the link settings temporarily; a follow-up run confirmed `app.json` is byte-identical before and after. The others are most likely rewritten by Obsidian on relaunch, though I had no before-copy to diff them against. `community-plugins.json` lists both `discourse-graphs` and `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; the stray folder name probably predates this work.

**Things to know**
- **Watcher warnings:** every run warned about the `eng-2279` worktree's watcher and the main checkout's own `scripts/dev.ts` watcher (pid 92351). The `main.js` hash stayed the same during every run, so no run was marked invalid.
